D: A student's vision gets him and a handful of classmates off their flight to Paris, but death has a plan, and they're all on it.
P: Serve the croque monsieur bites when the class boards Flight 180 for Paris.
S: Paris class trip croque monsieur bites
the senior class's first taste of France, before take-off

Melt the butter, stir in the flour, whisk in the milk and simmer to a thick béchamel. Season with the nutmeg and salt. Heat the grill. Spread 4 slices of bread with mustard, top with the ham and half the gruyère and close the sandwiches. Toast in a dry frying pan until golden on both sides. Spread the béchamel over the tops, scatter with the rest of the gruyère and grill until bubbling. Cut each into 4 squares.
packed for the long flight across the Atlantic

Cook the onions in the butter and oil with the salt over low heat, stirring often, until deep golden and jammy. Cool. Beat the sour cream and cream cheese until smooth and fold in the onions, most of the chives and the pepper. Chill so the flavours settle. Scatter with the rest of the chives and serve with the crisps.
M: the hot dinner service on the overnight route to Paris

Season the chicken with the salt and pepper and brown skin side down in the oil in a wide heavy pan, then turn, brown and lift out. Fry the bacon, onions and mushrooms in the same pan until golden, then add the garlic. Stir in the flour and tomato paste, pour in 500ml red wine and 250ml chicken stock, and add the thyme and bay. Return the chicken skin side up, cover and simmer gently. Uncover and simmer until the sauce coats a spoon. Scatter with parsley and serve with torn baguette.
W: served at the funeral home, with a quiet word of warning

Whisk the eggs, caster sugar, honey and lemon zest until pale and thick. Fold in the flour and baking powder, then 100g of the melted butter. Cover and chill the batter. Heat the oven to 200C and brush a madeleine tray with the rest of the butter. Spoon in the batter and bake until domed and golden. Turn out, dust with icing sugar and serve warm.
K: a toast to Paris, raised before the seatbelt sign goes off
Shake the gin, lemon juice and sugar syrup hard with the ice. Strain into 4 chilled flutes. Top with the sparkling wine and add a lemon twist.

Fry the onions and carrots in the rest of the oil until golden, then add the garlic, smoked paprika, salt and pepper.
Stir in the flour and tomato paste, pour in 500ml red wine and 250ml vegetable stock with the soy sauce, and add the thyme and bay.
Return the mushrooms and simmer uncovered until the carrots are tender and the sauce coats a spoon.
Scatter with parsley and serve with torn baguette.
